payload.title: [sfu-media-1] SFU join-token (HMAC auth nonce) is minted but never verified — token authorization is non-existent
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING sfu-media-1 (high/authz, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/calls/sfu-media-plane.ts
LINES: 196-214, 274-284

WHAT: issueJoinToken() mints a short-lived HMAC nonce (`#mintNonce`, line 279) documented (lines 44-50, 274-278) as the credential 'the client presents on its produce/consume calls' and which 'the server re-derives and checks (and the expiry)'. No such verification exists anywhere. There is no verifyNonce/verifyToken function in the repo (rg for timingSafeEqual / nonce-verify in calls/ returns nothing), and the produce/consume path in CallControlPlane.sfuProduce/sfuConsume/sfuConnectTransport (call-control-plane.ts:454-516) never accepts or checks the token — it only re-reads the participant record from the store. The gateway handlers (gateway.ts:1746-1793) also never pass a token. So the carefully minted, expiry-bound, per-(call,user,device) credential is dead weight: expiry is never enforced on the media path, and the HMAC binding is never used.

IMPACT: The advertised security control (short-lived, expiry-bound, cryptographically-bound join credential) provides zero protection. Token expiry is meaningless on produce/consume; a participant can keep producing/consuming long after token TTL. The only gate is the store participant check, so all real authorization rests on finding #2/#3, not on the token. Defense-in-depth that operators will assume exists does not.

SUGGESTED FIX: Either (a) remove the token from the grant and document that authz is store-backed, or (b) actually verify it: have sfuProduce/sfuConsume/sfuConnectTransport require the token, re-derive `${callId}:${userId}:${deviceId}:${expirySeconds}` HMAC-SHA256 with the secret, compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and reject expired/forged nonces before touching the backend.
